v1.feedback: The Tinguely concept lands — horizontal band slicing with per-band rotation is a legit mechanical-decomposition idea, not a rename. The 18s calm / 3.5s jam cycle is well-paced and the ramp envelope keeps it from feeling like a switch flip. Two things to tighten: the band slide amplitude (0.6) is modest enough that during jam the Lucy silhouette muddies into a vaguely banded blob rather than reading as a machine exploding its own armature — push slide to ~1.2 and widen band count to 16–20 so individual slices are thinner and more kinetic. Second, the palette shift from ivory to steel is too subtle at 0.7 mix — let it hit 1.0 during peak jam and add a brief desaturation pulse so the color swerve is unmistakable, not just a warmth tweak.

v2.feedback: The Tinguely-jam idea lands — horizontal band-sliding and per-band rotation genuinely evoke a kinetic-sculpture jam session, and the warm-ivory → steel-blue palette shift during the jam phase is a tasteful swerve that reads clearly. Two things hold it back: the jam window (3.5s every 18s) is too brief relative to the calm phase, so most of the time you're just watching a breathing Lucy — lengthen the jam to ~5-6s or add a secondary micro-tremor during calm so the machine never looks fully at rest. Also the camera is fixed at z=30 with a slow orbit; during peak jam the bands slide far enough that extremities clip toward frame edge on narrow viewports — either pull the camera back slightly during jam (lerp FOV or z) or clamp slide amplitude to keep the silhouette comfortably inside 85% of the frame.
